title: Throughput credibility harness, benchmarking methodology, and customer onboarding acceptance tests
creator: Priya Shah
description: Build a deterministic, tenant-aware load testing harness and a statistically rigorous benchmarking methodology to establish throughput credibility for Dedicated customers. Deliver an end-to-end customer acceptance test suite and onboarding playbook that product/security/solutions teams can run with customers. The work covers generator design, traffic shaping profiles (steady, ramp, microburst), seed determinism for reproducible runs, telemetry validation, pass/fail SLO matrix, artifact packaging (reports + reproducible manifests), and instructions for customer-run verification in their Dedicated environment.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic run: a canonical workload manifest plus random seed produces repeatable latency/throughput distributions across 5 independent runs (95th percentile variance < 3%)
Profile coverage: harness supports at least 5 profiles: low-throughput steady, high-throughput steady, 95th-tail microburst, tenant-mix replay, and cold-start ramp

Telemetry alignment: generated traffic maps to expected Redwood telemetry keys and dashboards (token_count, response_latency_p50/p95/p99, queue_depth, node_cpu, gpu_util) and alerts if telemetry drift > threshold
SLO matrix: automated report determines pass/fail against customer SLA matrix (throughput target, tail latency, error budget) and produces an artifact for signing
Onboarding guide: 1-page checklist + runnable scripts and a post-run verification script that customers can run in private deployments
Artifacts: produces a versioned report (CSV + JSON summary), Grafana dashboard snapshot link, and reproducible workload manifest stored in the artifacts bucket
notes: Design trade-off: keep generator language-agnostic (golang runner) to reduce GC jitter; provide lightweight python client for custom payloads
Decision: use seeded request timing and payload RNG to make runs reproducible; exclude downstream external calls by mocking external integrations in the harness
Telemetry sampling: enable full-span capture for first 30s of each run to validate request paths, then switch to sampled telemetry to reduce storage costs
Risk: hardware heterogeneity across Dedicated pools can inflate variance; mitigation: capture node fingerprint (GPU model, driver, kernel) and include in report
Customer UX: provide a "dry-run" mode that validates connectivity and permissions then a "certify" mode that runs full benchmark and packages artifacts
